clue.text: Tried a politician in Northern town with Department's head

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the name of the town, so the town wraps around it
the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Department is kept

blocks.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England
an MP is a Member of Parliament
first letter of Department

explanation.surface: Someone put a politician on trial in a northern English town, with a government department's chief alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' reads like a court verdict, but it means tested or tasted. Sale is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sampled something is to have tried a little of it, so the two past-tense verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Taking food in hospital to suppress temperature is wise

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so the hospital word goes around the food

blocks.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
a pie is food
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A patient fed in hospital to bring a fever down is acting sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to suppress' means to sit on top of: the hospital-with-food goes above the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary adjective for having great wisdom, from the Latin sapere, to be wise.

clue.text: Island's an alternative to a big house

blocks.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: An island makes a cheaper alternative to buying a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is the main house of a country estate, so a large house belonging to a landowner.

clue.text: Drunk most of huge gin with a large mug

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter is kept
a drunk is unsteady and jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has downed a huge gin poured into a large drinking mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a drinking vessel in the surface, but it is slang for the face or mouth. HUGE loses its E before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing gear is jocular British slang for the mouth, and mug is slang for the face or mouth.

clue.text: Model initially looks hurt and desperately upset

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is kept
upset means turned over, which in a down answer turns the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A fashion model at first appears injured and badly distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophie Dahl is an English former fashion model, granddaughter of the writer Roald Dahl.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names a profession, and Sophie Dahl is a well-known example of a model.

clue.text: Show without skirts makes you blush

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word sits around the second

blocks.note: to con is an archaic verb for to teach or study, hence to show
skirts as edges or borders, the way a path skirts a field

explanation.surface: A stage show performed with no skirts at all would make the audience go red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without skirts' looks like removing outer letters, but 'without' means outside here and 'skirts' gives a word for edges.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimson is to turn deep red, which is exactly what a face does when a person blushes; both are verbs.

clue.text: Actors into playing Scarfe, say

indicators.note: playing suggests acting out or fooling about, so the letters take on a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Actors are keen on portraying a famous satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerald Scarfe is an English satirical caricaturist, known for his political drawings and Pink Floyd's The Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarfe draws satirical caricatures, so he is an example of the profession, which 'say' signals.

clue.text: By spade there's old plant

blocks.note: a spade is a tool for digging, so working by spade is being in dig
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Next to a garden spade stands an ancient plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like next to, but 'by spade' is read as by means of digging, IN DIG; even the blogger found this part loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is the shrub whose leaves yield the blue dye of the same name, so it is a plant.

clue.text: It won't go down well with sponge trifle!

definitions.text: It won't go down well with sponge

blocks.clueFragment: It won't go down well with sponge
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a sponge is a heavy drinker, who would scorn weak ale
second meaning: something unimportant

explanation.walkthrough: Sponge and trifle suggest a pudding; but a sponge is a heavy drinker and a trifle is a matter of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means weak beer, disliked by serious drinkers, and figuratively a matter of little consequence.

clue.text: Suet can ruin fruitcake

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck its form, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Adding suet can spoil a fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' sits naturally beside suet as baking, but it is the slang for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is informal slang for a crazy person, and nutcase is a synonym in the same slang.

clue.text: Clerk has to write guide about opening of Parliament

indicators.note: about means going around, so the joined words surround the selected letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Parliament is used

blocks.note: to pen a letter is to write it
an usher guides people to their seats
first letter of Parliament

explanation.surface: An office clerk must write a guide on the state opening of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a dismissive name for a clerk or office worker whose job is routine paperwork.

clue.text: Plan a large collection at end of round

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of round is used

blocks.note: last letter of round
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A scheme to gather a big haul at the end of a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At end of round' places the large collection after the final letter of round.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline of a scheme, so it serves as a noun for a plan.

clue.text: Blue soil at end of rockery

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of rockery is used

blocks.note: earth is soil
last letter of rockery

explanation.surface: A gardener notes bluish soil at the far edge of a rock garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour, but it is the definition in its sense of crude or risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue humour is smutty, and earthy humour is coarse and frank about bodily matters, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Endlessly complain about odd lingo in the country

indicators.note: without its end, the word for complain loses its final letter
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put into a different order
about means surrounding, so the shortened complaint goes around the rearranged letters

blocks.note: to moan is to complain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller grumbles endlessly about the strange language spoken in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' looks like part of the surface's setting, but 'the country' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongolia is a landlocked nation in East Asia, an example of a country.

clue.text: Asian menus translated by stenographer

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so these letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shorthand typist renders Asian restaurant menus into English.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a person employed to take dictation or copy manuscripts, much like a stenographer.

clue.text: Sunday Times displayed in explosive meeting!

indicators.note: displayed in places the newspaper's self-reference inside the explosive

blocks.note: the newspaper printing the puzzle refers to itself as our name
TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive

explanation.surface: The newspaper's masthead features in coverage of a heated, explosive gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle was printed in the Sunday Times, so the paper's own title stands for the phrase 'our name'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting competition, a meeting of many players or teams over a series of contests.

clue.text: Happy with fluffy hair being crinkled?

blocks.note: feeling up means in good spirits
and joins things together, as with does
down is soft fine hair or feathers

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful about their soft hair being crimped into waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: a crinkled line goes repeatedly up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crinkled has ridges that rise and fall, so it runs in an undulating, wavy pattern.

clue.text: Nothing more than pool

blocks.note: first meaning: only
second meaning: a small lake or pond, as in Windermere

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a dismissive remark about a pool; the phrase and the noun are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means only or simply; as a poetic noun it means a lake or pond.

clue.text: American female – elegant and wealthy

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
F is the abbreviation for female
fluent means graceful and flowing, as in elegant prose

explanation.surface: A stylish, rich American woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means having plenty of money, so it is a synonym for rich or well off.

clue.text: See 3
Ambitious boss visits Indian state

the head is the boss

explanation.walkthrough: 'Visits' simply has the boss come after the state, so the pieces join in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person or firm is enterprising and keen to progress, so the adjective means ambitious.

clue.text: Sort of hand shuffled etc

indicators.note: cards that are shuffled change order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A card player describes a particular kind of hand being dealt, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc abbreviates et cetera, Latin for and the rest, which the English phrase and so forth translates.

clue.text: He suspends word game

blocks.note: first meaning: an executioner who hangs people
second meaning: the guessing game in which wrong letters build a gallows

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone halting a game of words; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the executioner who carries out a hanging and the pencil-and-paper spelling game.

clue.text: Starts to detest examiner during verbal test

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only the openings of the next two words are kept
during means within the span of, so the kept letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: oral means spoken, as verbal does
first letters of detest and examiner

explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial of endurance, and historically a trial by ordeal was a test of guilt.

blocks.note: outer letters of small
an oven is a cooker

clue.text: Temptingly display many fishes

clue.text: Hint of nausea follows foul-tasting bird

blocks.note: bitter means sharp or unpleasant in taste
first letter of nausea

explanation.surface: A trace of sickness comes after eating a bird that tasted foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the hint after the taste word, so it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading heron of reed beds, known for its booming call, so an example of a bird.
